title: Correctness of a query-state output
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a Boolean function, and let $\tau\in\mathbb{Q}$ satisfy $0<\tau\leq 1$. A query state is a correct output if there is a finite family $A$ of coordinate sets such that its active family is $A$, every Fourier coefficient of $f$ with magnitude at least $\tau$ is indexed by a set in $A$, every set in $A$ has Fourier coefficient magnitude greater than $\tau/2$, and $|A|$ is at most the active cap at threshold $\tau$ and at most $4/\tau^2$.
hypotheses_covered: Target is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube
State has an optional active family and a finite estimate trace
caveat: The active-cap function is referenced but not defined in the supplied definitions.
